title: Baked Ziti
shortDescription: Cheesy pasta bake for the table
subtitle: Cheesy pasta bake for the table
description: Cheesy pasta bake for the table. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Baked Ziti in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Yellow onion, diced, Fresh basil, chopped as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown beef and build sauce
steps.instruction: Brown ground beef in olive oil with onion until deeply colored. Add garlic and Italian seasoning; cook 1 minute. Stir in crushed tomatoes and marinara; simmer 15 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Par-cook ziti
steps.instruction: Boil ziti in salted water 3 minutes shy of al dente. Drain — baked ziti finishes in the oven, not the pot. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Mix ricotta filling
steps.instruction: Stir ricotta with half the parmesan, salt, and pepper until smooth. This layer keeps the bake creamy — skipping ricotta gives you red pasta, not baked ziti.

steps.title: Layer in hotel pans
steps.instruction: Spread half the meat sauce, then half the pasta, dollops of ricotta, and half the mozzarella. Repeat layers. Top with remaining sauce, mozzarella, and parmesan.

steps.title: Bake until bubbling
steps.instruction: Bake covered at 375°F 25 minutes, then uncover and bake 10–15 minutes until cheese browns at the edges. Rest 10 minutes before cutting — molten cheese needs to set.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Serve Baked Ziti
steps.instruction: Scoop squares from the pan onto sheet trays. Finish with basil. This is a cheesy pasta bake, not a cream-pasta toss. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Baked Ziti with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Baked Ziti on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Cheesy pasta bake for the table. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Any short pasta shape works — penne, rigatoni, or spaghetti.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Baked Ziti runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
